lines.text: Every satellite signal reaches the ground buried in natural noise.
A careful attacker can shape an attack to look exactly like that noise.
This is how it works, and how our ground-link testbed still catches it.
TerraSAR-X flies at 514 km and sends a fixed X-band carrier at 8477.8 MHz.
lines.say: Our satellite, Terra Sar X, flies at five hundred and fourteen kilometres, and sends a fixed X band carrier, at eight thousand, four hundred and seventy-seven point eight megahertz.

lines.text: The frequency is not random: it moves only with the Doppler shift, up to ±199 kHz, which the orbit predicts.
lines.say: The frequency is not random. It moves only with the Doppler shift, up to about two hundred kilohertz either way, and the orbit predicts it.

lines.text: At Zaghouan the carrier arrives between −88.8 and −74.4 dBm: an amplitude of 11.4 to 60.0 µV.
lines.say: At Zagwan, it arrives between minus eighty-eight point eight and minus seventy-four point four D B M: an amplitude of eleven point four to sixty microvolts.

lines.text: The receiver's noise floor is −100 dBm, so the signal-to-noise ratio runs from 11 to 26 dB over the pass.
lines.say: The noise floor is minus one hundred D B M, so the signal-to-noise ratio runs from eleven to twenty-six decibels.

lines.text: Natural noise has a signature.
Thermal noise is Gaussian and white: a flat floor across the band.
Against the orbit model, the carrier wanders by less than 20 Hz and the power by less than 1 dB.
lines.say: Against the orbit model, the carrier wanders by less than twenty hertz, and the power by less than one decibel.

lines.text: That narrow envelope is where an attacker has to hide.
One: noise-shaped jamming. Gaussian noise, raised slowly like a rain fade, so the floor creeps up instead of jumping.
Two: fade-mimicking spoofing. A rogue node matches the Doppler and adds fake fading, so its power sits only 3 dB low.
lines.say: Two: fade-mimicking spoofing. A rogue node matches the Doppler and adds fake fading, so its power sits only three decibels low.

lines.text: Three: bit flips disguised as channel errors. Chosen bits are flipped and the checksum recomputed, so the frame just looks noisy.
Our idea is to make every imitation either visible, or bounded: too small to cost the link more than about a decibel.
The physical layer is a chi-square engine: range, Doppler, power and phase are each compared with the orbit, in units of their natural spread.
lines.say: The physical layer is a chi-square engine. Range, Doppler, power and phase are each compared with the orbit, in units of their natural spread.

lines.text: To stay hidden overhead, injected noise must stay 5.3 dB below the thermal noise: at most 1.1 dB of signal-to-noise ratio, 1.7 dB at the 2° mask where the gate widens. Every frame still verifies.
lines.say: To stay hidden overhead, the injected noise must stay five point three decibels below the thermal noise. That is at most one point one decibels of signal-to-noise ratio, or one point seven at the two degree mask, where the gate widens. Every frame still verifies.

lines.text: Push harder, and the chi-square gate fires: a spoofer's 3 dB fade is 14 sigma off the link budget.
lines.say: Push harder, and the chi-square gate fires. A spoofer's three decibel fade is fourteen sigma off the link budget.

lines.text: The statistical layer is an Isolation Forest trained only on clean passes.
It reads what the chi-square cannot see: the constellation's error, lost frames, arrival jitter, failed tags, and how fast the carrier and power changed.
The data layer is cryptography, which noise cannot imitate: every frame carries an HMAC-SHA256 tag made with a secret key.
lines.say: The data layer is cryptography, which noise cannot imitate. Every frame carries an H MAC tag, made with a secret key.

lines.text: Change one bit, by accident or on purpose, and the tag breaks: the frame is dropped and requested again.
Either deterministic tier, data or physical, rejects a frame. When two tiers fire at once, the link is quarantined, and the key is changed only if someone holds it.
In our tests, every attack packet was flagged, and no corrupted frame reached the analyst.
About one and a half percent of genuine packets were held back for review.
Try it live on the testbed, in the dashboard folder of our code.
lines.say: Try it live, on our testbed.
